pageCache.pageTitle: Richard Cobden Primary School - British Values
pageCache.text:
School Online Payments
British Values
At Richard Cobden Primary School we are committed to ensuring our pupils receive a high quality education through an enriched curriculum that reflects the diversity of our community. We value and celebrate the diverse backgrounds of everyone at our school. We also value and celebrate being part of Britain. We place a high priority on helping our pupils to develop as confident and responsible citizens. In doing this, it is very important to us that our pupils have a clear understanding of their rights and responsibilities. This is achieved through the values, aims and ethos of our school, which are underpinned by the fundamental British values of:
The Department for Education have recently reinforced the need “to create and enforce a clear and rigorous expectation on all schools to promote the fundamental British values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty and mutual respect and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs.”
At our school we promote these values through our curriculum and curriculum enrichment, through spiritual, moral, social and cultural development, through personal, social, health and economic education, through religious education, and in the way in which we treat each other.
Democracy
The rule of law
Individual liberty
Democracy
Our pupils are given lots of opportunity to develop their understanding of democracy. As well as learning about the historical context through exciting topic based learning, they also get to experience it for themselves. Pupils have a clear voice in our school. The election of our school council enables them to nominate and vote for representatives for every year group, enabling all pupils to contribute their ideas and viewpoints. They also contribute their views through pupil surveys and this informs our school development priorities.
Each class and the school council hold their own budget, helping them to develop their understanding of decision making and compromise. They make decisions about which charities the school supports each year. Pupils help to agree the rules which enable us all to get along and work well together. All pupils are listened to by adults and they are taught to listen to each other carefully and to show concern for each other. They learn the importance of respecting the right of every individual to have their voices and opinions heard. We promote personal and social responsibility by encouraging pupils to be independent and to take personal responsibility for their learning and the impact of their behaviour on others.
The Rule of Law
The importance of laws in our society is reinforced throughout each school day. Pupils are taught the reasons why laws are necessary and the values they protect. Our pupils will encounter laws and rules throughout their lives. It is our responsibility to teach them the importance of laws and rules in governing and protecting us, and that they must be adhered to. The importance of laws and rules is consistently reinforced through lessons, assemblies, religious education, physical education, behaviour management and when pupils are devising class rules. Through their involvement in creating our rules, pupils develop an understanding of the reasons behind them, and the consequences if they are broken.
Pupils are given opportunities to discuss and debate the reasons for laws in order to help them understand how laws protect them. They are provided with a secure environment where, over the time they are with us, they can learn how to manage their own behaviour and its impact on others. Wherever possible, through a restorative approach, pupils are given the opportunity to put right any wrong they have done. This helps to develop their ability to take responsibility for their actions. Through their treatment at our school, pupils learn the importance of a fair system where actions are clearly explained. We work with community partners such as the police, fire brigade and health care professionals to help pupils learn how to keep themselves safe from harm. Pupils are helped to understand that while different people may hold different views about what is ‘right’ and ‘wrong’, all people living in England are subject to its law.
Individual Liberty
Through our secure and supportive environment where we have established sensible boundaries, and we provide ongoing guidance, we actively encourage our pupils to make independent choices and take responsibility for them. Through our everyday provision, including PSHEE and e-safety learning, pupils are encouraged to exercise their rights and freedoms, and they are supported to learn how to do this safely. They learn how to express their opinions and beliefs, how to do this with due regard for the feelings of others, and to respect the rights of others to do likewise. We place a high priority on developing the social and emotional aspects of learning. Through this we support pupils to develop the confidence and self-esteem to make their needs and feelings known. We help pupils to interpret social interaction and to understand the emotions of others.
We recognise that some pupils will often experience difficult life challenges which impact on their individual liberties. Through our supportive provision and our close partnerships with other agencies, we work tirelessly to help pupils and their families.
Mutual respect and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs
Richard Cobden School is a very diverse community and as such it provides a rich environment for developing pupils’ understanding of the importance of mutual respect and tolerance. This is embedded in our values, our curriculum, our assemblies, our behaviour management procedures, religious education, PSHEE teaching, in the daily interactions between adults and pupils, and the relationships pupils have with each other. Our pupils know and understand our expectation that respect and tolerance is shown to everyone, whatever differences we may have. Through our curriculum and by celebrating different faiths and cultures, we actively promote diversity and reinforce the values of tolerance and respect for others. Children are encouraged to discuss and show tolerance of differences between people such as their faith, ethnicity, gender, disability, sexual orientation or family structure. They learn that their behaviour has an effect on their own rights and those of others.
Sadly, no school can guarantee that there will never be instances which are contrary to fundamental British values. We respect everyone’s right to hold different viewpoints. However, we will actively challenge opinions or behaviors in school that are contrary to fundamental British values, including ‘extremist’ views, as these are at odds with the values of Richard Cobden School.
British Values

pageCache.text:
School Online Payments
Year 6 Breakfast with Maths at UCS
Our Year 6 pupils took part in a special “Breakfast with Maths” session at UCS on Wednesday, 3rd December. The visit included a shared breakfast and an inspiring mentoring workshop led by UCS staff and students.
The children engaged in challenging mathematical problems, collaborative activities, and had the chance to experience learning in a secondary-school environment. It was a fantastic morning full of curiosity, confidence and brilliant ideas — a great start to this new partnership with UCS.

pageCache.pageTitle: Richard Cobden Primary School - Richard Cobden Pupils Win Reading Competition at The Hall School
pageCache.text:
School Online Payments
Richard Cobden Pupils Win Reading Competition at The Hall School
On Wednesday 17th June 2026, six pupils from Years 4, 5 and 6 proudly represented Richard Cobden Primary School at a reading competition hosted by The Hall School in Highgate.
Our representatives — Maysa from 6J, Ameerah from 6I, Norah from 5B, Aurora from 5L, Fatima and Maryam from 4C — were chosen after winning their individual class competitions. They then went on to take part in the finals against pupils from four other Camden primary schools.
The standard of the competition was extremely high, with all participants demonstrating excellent expression, tone, articulation and pace in their reading. After a very impressive final, the judges announced Richard Cobden Primary School as the overall winner.
We were also delighted that Fatima, Norah and Ameerah won their individual year group competitions for Years 4, 5 and 6. This was a fantastic achievement and a very proud moment for our school.
Well done to all six pupils for their hard work, confidence and wonderful reading. You have made Richard Cobden extremely proud!

pageCache.pageTitle: Richard Cobden Primary School - Celebrating Culture and Community at our Summer Fair!
pageCache.text:
School Online Payments
Celebrating Culture and Community at our Summer Fair!
What happens when you mix bouncy castles, samosas, glittery face paint, penalty shootouts, crafts, and a rat that needs catching? You get an unforgettable day at Richard Cobden! Our Culture Day and Summer Fair was a joyful celebration of fun, food and community spirit – and it couldn’t have happened without the incredible support of our Parents’ Association, families, staff and, of course, our wonderful children.
The playground came alive with delicious food stalls offering a mouth-watering selection of traditional dishes lovingly prepared by parents (we’re still thinking about them), two bouncy castles in full bounce mode, and a fantastic range of activities – from Catch the Rat and Beat the Buzzer to book stalls, throwing games and an epic penalty shootout with staff in goal (still recovering).
Face-painting and crafts added colour and sparkle to the day – we had tigers, butterflies and superheroes roaming the fair, proudly painted and glittered.
It was a huge success, full of laughter, good food, community warmth and a lot of fun.
A massive thank you to everyone who was involved – the Parents’ Association, all the helping hands, our brilliant staff and – most of all – our children, without whom none of this would matter.
They had a blast – and that’s what it’s all about.

KS2 Sports Day – Team Spirit and Sunshine!
Children from Years 4, 5 and 6 had an action-packed Sports Day on our school pitch, filled with energy, determination and lots of cheering! Pupils took part in a range of exciting athletic events, including throwing, long jump, speed bounce and sprints – showing great sportsmanship and effort throughout the day.
The competition was close, but it was Eversholt (Green Team) who came out on top as this year’s winners – well done! A big thank you to all the staff who helped make the day such a success, and to our fantastic children for giving it their all with such enthusiasm.

pageCache.text:

Year 6 Visit to the Science Museum
Year 6 pupils from both classes enjoyed an exciting visit to the Science Museum in South Kensington. During the trip, children explored interactive galleries, investigated forces, energy and engineering, and took part in hands-on activities that brought science to life.
A highlight of the visit was a practical workshop, where pupils worked in groups, used scientific equipment and developed their enquiry skills through observation, testing and discussion.
The children showed curiosity, teamwork and excellent behaviour throughout the day. It was a fantastic opportunity to connect classroom learning with real-life science and technology.

Christmas Lunch at School 🎄
Our pupils enjoyed a wonderful Christmas lunch together with their teachers and staff members, creating a truly festive atmosphere across the school. Children had the opportunity to try a delicious selection of traditional Christmas dishes prepared by our fantastic kitchen team.
The hall was beautifully decorated, the children looked fabulous in their festive outfits, and many proudly wore crowns they had made themselves. It was a special time to sit, eat and celebrate together, sharing joy, laughter and the spirit of Christmas.
A lovely moment of togetherness for our whole school community.

pageCache.pageTitle: Richard Cobden Primary School - Year 6 Visit to the British Museum
pageCache.text:
School Online Payments
Year 6 Visit to the British Museum
Our Year 6 classes, Jacaranda and Iroko, recently visited the British Museum to explore the fascinating Benin Bronzes. The trip allowed the children to extend their knowledge from lessons at school and to connect it with their writing project, “Children of the Benin Kingdom.”
The exhibition gave pupils the opportunity to see the incredible craftsmanship of the Benin artists and to learn more about the rich and mysterious history of the Kingdom of Benin. The children were amazed by the detail and beauty of the bronzes, especially those showing interactions between the Benin people and Portuguese traders.
During the visit, the pupils also had a chance to sketch some of their favourite artefacts, observe differences between the various bronzes, and reflect on what they had learned in class. It was an inspiring experience that brought history to life! We would also like to thank the parents for helping us!

Year 6 Iroko and Jacaranda – Junior Citizen Day
This week, our Year 6 Jacaranda and Iroko classes took part in the Junior Citizen workshop in Kentish Town. The event was part of the Junior Citizenship Scheme, supported by Transport for London, which helps children learn how to stay safe and make sensible decisions in real-life situations.
During the visit, the pupils met with police officers, firefighters, and paramedics who shared important lessons about personal safety, emergency response, and being responsible members of the community. It was a fun and engaging experience that helped our Year 6 children develop confidence, independence, and key life skills as they prepare for their move to secondary school.

Richard Cobden Primary School – Takeover Challenge 2025
Pupils from Richard Cobden Primary School took part in Camden’s annual Takeover Challenge on 21 November 2025 at the Crowndale Centre. Our school focused on Online Safety, with children sharing clear and thoughtful ideas about how young people can stay safe, responsible and confident online.
The event brought together pupils from eight Camden primary schools to explore key themes such as online safety, SEND inclusion, children’s rights and mental health.
Our presentation was delivered to senior Camden leaders, including Councillor Marcus Boyland and the Mayor of Camden, Councillor Eddie Hanson, along with representatives from Camden Learning. We are extremely proud of our pupils for their creativity, insight and strong voice in this important borough-wide discussion.

Year 6 Iroko & Jacaranda – Benin Bronzes Art Project
Both Year 6 classes, Iroko and Jacaranda, took part in a unique two-day art project last week, exploring the history and artistic traditions of the Benin Bronzes. Building on their earlier learning in humanities, pupils created their own artworks inspired by the rich heritage of the Benin Kingdom.
The workshops were led by Alix Smith, an experienced artist-teacher who brought her creativity, expertise and passion for visual arts directly into our classrooms. The sessions were highly engaging and hands-on, and our pupils showed curiosity, imagination and excellent teamwork throughout. Their final pieces reflect a deepening understanding of global art, culture and storytelling.

Year 1, 2 and 3 Winter Show ❄️
Our Year 1, 2 and 3 children delighted audiences with a wonderful Winter Show, performed three times — once for the whole school and twice for parents. The performances were full of joy, confidence and festive spirit, and were warmly received by everyone who attended.
The show attracted great interest, with long-lasting applause at the end of each performance. It was a special and memorable experience for the children, their families and the wider Richard Cobden Primary School community, celebrating creativity, teamwork and the joy of performing together.

A Wonderful Christmas Surprise at Our School 🎅✨
Today, our pupils enjoyed a wonderful surprise at school – they were visited by Santa Claus! Every child received a small gift that brought lots of joy and smiles. In addition, the children were able to take part in various fun games and activities, which they joined in with great enthusiasm.
This special event was organised by the members of our Parents Association, and we would like to express our heartfelt thanks for their time, effort and kindness in preparing such a magical experience for our children.
We wish everyone a joyful and relaxing holiday break, and we look forward to seeing you all in the New Year! 🎄✨
